problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods (VLFM, WMNav, SG-Nav) handle only a single target, and LLM-based planners for multi-step tasks (InstructNav) re-query at every step, ignore temporal constraints and give no formal guarantees. Existing value maps also assign one direction-agnostic score across the whole FOV.
motivation: Real household commands such as 'Clean either the chair or the couch, then turn on the tv' need multiple targets, ordering, and disjunction in unknown environments. Formal automata make constraint satisfaction verifiable and support online replanning, and per-direction VLM scoring gives finer spatial guidance for exploration.
key_idea: Compile the natural language command into LTL with one LLM call, convert it to a DFA whose weighted shortest path dynamically picks the active target over per-target multi-channel value maps, and score labeled frontier directions with the VLM (directional score) for exploration.
insight: Reducing multi-step temporal reasoning to one-shot NL-to-LTL translation plus graph search gives constraint-satisfying plans by construction. In the planner-only benchmark, ViTL completes up to 95.3% (capped by translation accuracy) versus 88.3% for a GPT-5.2 LLM-planner, whose failures are constraint violations and premature 'Done'. Directional score gives +1.7 SR over VLFM at similar SPL, but there is no isolated ablation of its components.
method: NL-to-LTL compilation: a single LLM call extracts target categories and temporal constraints into an LTL formula, and action verbs are reduced to 'reach'
DFA construction: the LTL is compiled to a DFA with lomap; edges correspond to reaching target objects, and the DFA state advances only on reaching

Dynamic target selection: edge weights are w_det<<1 for detected targets, w_fail>>1 for failed ones and 1.0 otherwise; Dijkstra shortest path to the accepting state picks the next target and replans when D, R or B changes; infeasibility is detected when the path cost reaches w_fail
Multi-channel value maps: one value map per target category, all updated in parallel so exploration knowledge is kept across target switches

Directional score: frontiers are projected onto the RGB image with letter labels plus an 'explore elsewhere' option; the VLM's next-token softmax over letters gives P(f_i), which is multiplied by a Yes/No scene score S_curr
Smooth value map: scene-weighted temporal fusion of old and new values, then angle-based linear interpolation across the FOV cone with virtual edge frontiers (attenuation β)
Frontier selection and control: pick the frontier with the max value in radius r on the active channel and execute it with a pre-trained depth PointNav policy

setting.backbone: LLaVA-NeXT-34B (frozen, 8-bit) for scoring; YOLOv7-E6E detector; GPT-5.2 for NL-to-LTL; pretrained PointNav policy (from VLFM)
setting.action_space: discrete move_forward 0.25 m / turn_left 30° / turn_right 30° / stop, with frontier waypoints executed by a PointNav policy
setting.privileged: none (task-level planner benchmark uses a probabilistic executor model; full-system eval uses two selected scenes)

numbers_note: Planner results (95.3% NL-to-LTL accuracy, 88.3% LLM-planner completion) and path length 25.45 m vs 30.05 m are on the paper's own benchmark, with the sweep only in figures; not put in numbers.
results: On HM3D ObjectNav v2 (2000 episodes) ViTL reaches 54.1 SR / 30.9 SPL, beating VLFM (52.4/30.8) and SG-Nav-GPT (54.0/24.9) in SR/SPL balance, but trailing WMNav Gemini 1.5 Pro (58.1/31.2) in SR. The planner completes tasks with 95.3% translation accuracy against 88.3% for a GPT-5.2 LLM-planner, with fewer exploration attempts. On 50 mutually completed episodes in two scenes, paths are 15.31% shorter (25.45 m vs 30.05 m).
limitations: Each sub-task is reduced to reaching an object, so manipulation or interaction is not handled
Task-level evaluation uses a synthetic benchmark with a probabilistic executor, and the end-to-end multi-target test is small (2 scenes, 50 episodes); no end-to-end multi-target SR is reported
Correctness relies on NL-to-LTL translation (95.3%); no ablation of directional score components; simulation only
